title: Using AI to Actually Learn — Module Quiz

items.q: Why does a clear explanation frequently fail to produce learning?
options: Ease of following is mistaken for the ability to reproduce it
items.explain: Recognition feels like knowledge. People rate understanding highest right after a fluent account and perform worse than that later.

items.q: A desirable difficulty is:
options: A topic that is genuinely hard
Effort during learning that feels worse but improves later retention
items.explain: Testing, spacing and mixing topics all degrade study-time performance and improve what remains.

items.q: The reliable test of understanding is:
options: Re-reading and checking it still makes sense
Explaining it aloud from memory with everything closed
items.explain: Where you stall is the boundary of your understanding, and it is invisible while the text is in front of you.

items.q: Better than 'explain it simply' is:
options: Stating what you already understand so it can build from there
items.explain: New understanding attaches to existing understanding, and 'simply' is pitched at nobody in particular.

items.q: When given an analogy you should always ask:
options: Where it breaks down and what it would mislead you about
Whether it is the standard one
items.explain: Every analogy is wrong somewhere, and not knowing where is how it calcifies into a misconception.

items.q: Asking for the same idea explained a second, different way reveals:
options: Whether the first explanation was accurate
Whether you understood the idea or memorised a phrasing
items.explain: If both land and you can see they describe the same thing, you have the idea rather than one wording of it.

items.q: Re-reading is ineffective mainly because:
options: It builds familiarity without retrieving anything from memory
items.explain: The text looks known, so you conclude you know it — the fluency illusion arriving through the commonest study habit.

items.q: The testing effect means:
options: Retrieving from memory strengthens it more than reviewing does
items.explain: Testing is the method of learning rather than a measurement of it — including the attempts you get wrong.

items.q: The most common way people get nothing from self-testing:
options: Using questions that are too hard
Reading the question, thinking 'I know that', and moving on
items.explain: That is recognition wearing retrieval's clothes. The answer must be produced in full before anything is revealed.

items.q: A poor practice question is one that:
options: Requires applying the idea to a new situation
Can be answered by recognising the right option
items.explain: Elimination lets you be right while recalling nothing, which is why open recall and error-finding are better shapes.

items.q: Spacing beats cramming because:
options: Partial forgetting makes the next retrieval effortful, and the effort strengthens it
items.explain: You rebuild the memory rather than topping it up — which is why a review that felt too easy was slightly wasted.

items.q: The commonest reason people abandon a review system:
options: Too many cards, creating a backlog
items.explain: The cure is a smaller deck rather than more discipline — cards only for what you would mind forgetting in six months.

items.q: Flashcards are poorly suited to building:
options: Understanding, judgement and the ability to do something
items.explain: No number of cards teaches you to diagnose a fault or structure an argument.

items.q: Teaching exposes gaps that reading does not because:
options: Producing an explanation requires making the connections yourself
items.explain: Reading only requires following connections somebody else made. The bridges are where understanding lives.

items.q: Why forbid the assistant from explaining or correcting during teach-back?
options: It will otherwise finish your explanation or agree, collapsing the exercise
items.explain: Do not explain, do not correct yet, be confused where a beginner would be — all three are load-bearing.

items.q: Reaching for jargon while explaining usually signals:
options: Using the term instead of understanding the idea
items.explain: Alongside 'it just does' and explanations that lengthen as you circle something you cannot state.

items.q: The deepest limitation of an assistant as a teacher:
options: It cannot see what you do not know, so it never reaches the gap you cannot ask about
items.explain: It answers the question you asked, and that question is bounded by what you already know.

items.q: Why is agreeableness especially dangerous for a learner?
options: If it concedes to your pushback you cannot tell which version was right
items.explain: You have been taught your misconception was correct, by something that sounded certain both times.

items.q: What compensates for an assistant having no curriculum?
options: Taking the sequence from a syllabus, textbook or course and working inside it
items.explain: Knowing which order a subject needs is part of knowing the subject, so a learner cannot supply it.

items.q: Skills like writing, diagnosis and design resist explanation because:
options: They are too complex to explain
The knowledge lives in trained reactions built by repetition and feedback
items.explain: Reactions are trained by exposure rather than told, so there is nothing to transfer as explanation.

items.q: The specific risk created by making explanation more efficient:
options: Spending months learning about something and never doing it
items.explain: Reading is comfortable and measurable, and produces confident half-knowledge you will not test until it matters.

items.q: Why does an explanation land better after a failed attempt?
options: The attempt creates a hook the explanation attaches to
You read more carefully when frustrated
items.explain: Hence the order: explain briefly, attempt badly, get feedback, then explain again at what went wrong.

items.q: The study loop's proportions should be:
options: One part explanation, three parts producing something
items.explain: Most people's study is the reverse, which feels better and works less well.

items.q: Self-directed learning is usually abandoned because:
options: Nothing external holds it in place
items.explain: An assistant has no stake in whether you continue, so the fixed time, the thing that expects you and the visible record must come from you.

items.q: "Is this cheating?" contains two separate questions:
options: Is it detectable, and is it common?
Does it break the rules I am under, and does it defeat the point of the work?
Is it allowed, and is it useful?
items.explain: You can break rules while learning a great deal, and follow every rule while learning nothing.

items.q: The test for whether AI use defeats the purpose of a task:
options: How much of the text you produced
Whether the thing the task was designed to produce in you actually happened
items.explain: Adding a check to your own thinking is safe; replacing your thinking with output is not.

items.q: AI-detection tools are unreliable in a specific way:
options: They produce false positives disproportionately for non-native English writers
They only work on long documents
items.explain: A plainer, more regular register gets flagged for being plain — so keep drafts and version history.
